_DataExportV2.description:
Export v2: the full per-user data set (S-021).

The audit found the portability response omitted notes, notifications,
chapter progress, revision items, the AI-usage ledger and analytics events
-- all stored per user -- while ``DELETE /users/me`` cascaded through
every one of them. A data subject received a partial answer to "what do
you hold about me". F-040 added the graded-answer record (``answer_log``),
the AI-memory preferences (``learning_prefs``/``memory_enabled``) and the
per-attempt ``quiz_json``; v1's four sections and v2's table list are
otherwise unchanged, so the version marker stays "2".

Extending the schema in a local subclass keeps the served OpenAPI document
honest (the versioned endpoint really returns these fields) without
touching ``schemas.py``.

Credential material is deliberately NOT exported: ``password_resets`` and
``email_verifications`` appear as metadata rows without their token
hashes. Shared library artifacts (``chapter_contents`` authored by this
account) are also out of scope -- they are not personal data once another
school reads them -- and staff-only handling fields (feedback
``triage_note``) are omitted.
_DataExportV2.title: _DataExportV2

Retention sweep (D20, ): expired tokens, stale invites, old chats.

``chat_retention_days`` are deleted with their messages. With
``dry_run=true`` the SAME count report is returned without deleting
anything (compliance evidence); real runs also write the audit row.

confirmation -- ``?confirm=true`` or an ``X-Confirm-Purge: true``
header. A dry run is always allowed (it is the compliance-safe path and
the one an operator should run first). A refused call writes no audit
row (nothing happened) but is logged, and the refusal names the missing
confirmation so a scripted caller cannot silently no-op. The sweep
itself stays idempotent: it only ever deletes rows past their window,
so a repeat after a successful run is a no-op with all-zero counts.

schema.title: Response Forgot Password Auth Forgot Post

post.description:
the holder of an impersonation token ends the session NOW.

The jti lands in the revocation cache with a TTL equal to the token's
remaining life, so the token stops working at once and the cache entry
itself disappears when the token would have expired anyway. Only works
with an impersonation token -- a normal session token cannot 'exit'
itself into 401s (that would be a self-DoS foot-gun).

Redeem a staff invite: create the account in the school and sign in.

Invite codes are single-use and time-limited; only their SHA-256 hash is
stored, and redemption is atomic (AUD-0034).

End THIS session now (S-011).

The presented token's jti is parked in the fail-closed revocation store
with a TTL matching the token's remaining life, so it stops
authenticating immediately instead of living out its 60-minute expiry
(a password change rotates the epoch for ALL sessions; this is the
per-session kill switch). Every token carries a jti; one that does not
is a legacy mint and is refused — silently accepting it would let a
caller believe a session was ended when it was not.

F-146: the namespace must match the token's claims. An impersonation
token is checked against ``imp_revoke:`` in ``get_current_user``, so
writing ``revoke:`` for it answered 204 while the token kept working —
a dishonest sign-out. The matching namespace is written, and any
impersonation window this admin session OPENED is ended with it (the
support window is a subset of the session that authorised it). The
implicit end is audited, so the trail shows why those tokens stopped.

schema.title: Response Mfa Disable Auth Mfa Disable Post
Response Mfa Verify Auth Mfa Verify Post

202.description: Generic accepted envelope; returned instead of 201/409 when REGISTRATION_EMAIL_CONFLICT=generic (F-143)

post.description:
Slide the session forward: mint a fresh token for the caller (B-02).

The web client renews PROACTIVELY while the presented token still
verifies -- a 40-minute class session on one login used to hard-expire
at minute 60 and bounce the user to /login, losing a quiz in progress.
An EXPIRED token cannot renew: this is fail-secure by construction (a
renewal grace window is a replay window; the proactive client contract
is what keeps honest users out of it). The returned token carries a new
jti and a full ``jwt_expire_minutes`` from now; the old token dies of
natural causes at its own expiry and is not force-revoked -- revoking
it would kill an in-flight request racing this renewal.

MFA step-up tokens are rejected as API credentials upstream (the
CurrentUser dependency answers before this runs); impersonation tokens
must NOT renew -- the 15-minute impersonated window is that design's
safety bound, so this route refuses them explicitly.

Re-send the email-verification code.

Reachable both with and without a session: login issues no token
for unverified accounts, so an authed-only resend left users stuck
at ``email_unverified`` with a link that always 401'd. When a
session is present it wins; otherwise ``payload.email`` identifies
the account. Always answers 202 with a generic body so the endpoint
cannot be used to enumerate registered addresses.

delete.description:
Revoke a live guardian invite code (F-145).

A leaked code used to stay redeemable for its full ``invite_ttl_minutes``
because only expiry or redemption could invalidate it, and no endpoint
existed to kill it deliberately. Revocation stamps ``used_at`` -- the
same single-use marker redemption writes -- so the code dies immediately
while the row survives as evidence that it existed and was killed rather
than redeemed.

Only the student who issued it may revoke it, and the answer is the same
404 whether the invite never existed or belongs to someone else, so the
endpoint cannot be used to probe invite ids. Idempotent: revoking an
already-dead code is a 204 (the desired end state already holds).

delete.description:
GDPR-style self-service account deletion.

Removes the account and every row owned by it: student/teacher/parent
profile and ALL FK-children (Postgres enforces referential integrity --
SQLite silently does not, so every child table must be cleaned here or
the delete aborts mid-transaction on the production engine). The last
remaining admin cannot delete their own account (409).

F-142: erasure is irreversible, so the CURRENT PASSWORD must be
re-supplied in the body — a bearer token alone (possibly a stolen
60-minute one) used to be enough to destroy the account permanently.
A missing body or wrong password is a coded 401, the same contract as
/auth/mfa/disable; a body-stripping intermediary therefore fails SAFE
(no deletion), never open.

Refused from an impersonated session: a support session is 15 minutes
and read-shaped, the erasure is forever, and the erased student cannot
be restored to check what the admin saw.

The erasure is the most destructive action in the product, so it leaves
an audit row (actor + target) *before* the account rows go. AuditLog
survives by design — its pointers to the erased account are anonymised
inside erase_account_everything — which is what makes a DSR review or an
incident post-mortem possible at all.

get.description: Self-service data portability: everything stored about this account.

post.description:
Sign out EVERYWHERE (S-011): stamps the token epoch, so every
outstanding bearer token of this account fails the F-05 epoch check on
its next request. DB-backed, so it holds even when the shared cache is
unreachable and survives restarts — the account-wide counterpart to
POST /auth/logout (which ends exactly one session).

Refused from an impersonated session (F-146 scope limit): revoking the
account's sessions is a destructive account-state change that outlives
the 15-minute support window. Ending the ADMIN session also ends the
impersonation windows it opened (the jti index in
``auth.impersonation``), which is why the presented token's jti is read
here.
